rows.gloss: All people are equal in dignity.
rows.subject: 人人
rows.because: stative predicate (Chinese adjectives are a verb subclass functioning as predicates with no copula) — copula-rule-4 analog; 在尊严上 is a locative adjunct, not the object

alternate.because: same undecided universal-quantification-promotion question as the Arabic and Swahili row 2 parallels

rows.anchor: 人人在尊严上一律平等。

rows.gloss: Everyone has the right to life.
rows.subject: 人人
rows.because: yǒu (has) is a possession verb — Relate·Structure, durable entitlement over the whole kind; matches the Arabic construction's CON·Pattern for the same proposition via a genuinely different (overt-verb, not prepositional) grammar

rows.gloss: No one shall be held in slavery.
rows.subject: 任何人
rows.because: núyì (enslave) binds the patient into a possession-relation — Relate·Structure, one person's status, Figure grain; polarity − from 不得 (R6); deontic 不得 noted, does not itself move the phasepost (A3). Genuinely diverges from the Arabic row 4 reading (SIG·Figure) because Mandarin's passive construction makes 'enslave' itself the main verb, where Arabic's construction makes 'is-permitted' the main verb over a nominalized 'enslavement' — same proposition, different finite verb, different phasepost, disclosed rather than forced to agree

rows.gloss: Everyone has the right to a nationality.
rows.subject: 人人
rows.because: yǒu quán (has the right) — same possession construction as row 3

rows.gloss: Everyone has the right to freedom of thought.
rows.subject: 人人
rows.because: yǒu (has) — same possession construction as rows 3 and 5
